key_insight: A drilled-to-bossed faying-surface geometry, combined with tuned DDFW parameters, substantially improves AA2024-T351 joint strength and is well captured by deep learning predictors.
engineering_relevance: The study offers a practical route to stronger lightweight aluminum welds for aerospace and automotive structures while also demonstrating data-driven process optimization for welding.
method: L18 orthogonal array testing of friction pressure, forging pressure, spindle speed, geometry, and friction time
Direct drive friction welding trials on a customized engine lathe
Deep learning comparison using an ensemble residual network, compact attention network, and adaptive multiscale network
evidence_signal: The best setting (30 MPa friction pressure, 70 MPa forging pressure, 2200 rpm, drilled-to-bossed geometry, 4 min) achieved 538 MPa tensile strength and 325 MPa torsional strength, and the best model reached about R² = 0.81 for tensile-strength prediction.
watch_item: The predictive accuracy is moderate rather than near-perfect, so broader validation on additional weld conditions and independent datasets would be needed before deployment.
paper_title: Enhancing weld performance of AA2024-T351 using drilled-to-bossed geometry and deep learning prediction in direct drive friction welding
